newsitem.title: CHINA: China honours Mao victim, omits blame.
newsitem.headline: China honours Mao victim, omits blame.

text.p: China on Saturday heaped posthumous praise on one of its former military commanders but failed to mention his sacking and death in disgrace after daring to criticise Mao Zedong.
The official media gave prominent coverage to a ceremony marking the publication of a book on Marshal Peng Dehuai, one of Chairman Mao's most prominent victims.

Peng was purged in 1959 after he clashed with Mao at the pivotal meeting of communist leaders at Lushan, the cool mountain resort in Jiangxi province which triggered heated debate over some of China's most disastrous economic errors.
Peng, defence minister at the time, criticised Mao's misguided Great Leap Forward, saying that many of the claimed successes of the drive to spur rapid development had been greatly inflated.
He was jailed in 1966 and died in prison eight years later.
The official People's Daily praised Peng for playing a major role in the Communist Party's history, only obliquely mentioning the fate that befell him.
"He was open and straightforward, standing for truth and enduring humiliation while carrying out an important mission," the newspaper said.
Peng was one of 10 Chinese communist military leaders to attain the rank of marshal.
The ceremony in Beijing was attended by top military leaders, including both vice chairmen of the powerful Central Military Commission, General Liu Huaqing and General Zhang Zhen.
